newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Kim orders steps to aid Hanbo Steel.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Kim orders steps to aid Hanbo Steel.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam on Friday ordered steps to allow debt-stricken Hanbo Steel Co to continue production, a statement from the presidential Blue House said.
The move came as state prosecutors grilled founder Chung Tae-soo of the Hanbo Group over a loan scandal surrounding its steelmaking unit.
"Steps should be taken to aid smooth production at Hanbo Steel plants which are already operational," Kim told a meeting with economic ministers.
"A fair assessment must be made of the mill under construction and it should be completed as scheduled if it proves to be feasible," he said.

Hanbo Steel, flagship of South Korea's 14th largest conglomerate, defaulted on debt repayments last week after piling up about five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans from 61 banks and financial institutions.
State prosecutors said they were questioning Chung and officials of Hanbo and creditor banks on how billions of dollars were funnelled to the financially shaky Hanbo Steel.
